## <a id="pkg-overview"></a>Overview

Package hottyedit edits a text field as a hotty host edits one (SPEC §10.2), for a program that draws its fields in cells: the same actions, the same words and lines, the same caret.

A program gives its surfaces a keymap in data-keys (hotty.TerminalKeys, say), and its cells rendition looks keys up in the same keymap, resolved with hotty.Resolve, and does what they say to a Field:

```go
km := hotty.Resolve(hotty.Platform{}, false, hotty.TerminalKeys)
f := hottyedit.Field{Value: "foo bar"}
switch a, changed := f.Key(km, "ctrl+w"); {
case a == "":
	// the program's key
case a == hotty.Submit:
	// submit the form
case changed:
	// report the input
}
```

A field has a selection, from its anchor to the caret, as a host's does: Key extends it with a move whose key has shift (hotty.Keymap.Selects), select-all selects the whole value, and Select sets it for the pointer. Selection says what to draw as selected.

Characters are grapheme clusters (Unicode UAX #29): the caret counts them.

A field keeps a history, for Undo and Redo, one step to a run of typing.

Undo and Redo are on where they were the program's before (hotty-go 0.7.2). A program that wants ctrl+z for itself binds it to Program in its keymap: Key then returns that action and the field leaves the key alone. A Field is comparable; its zero value is an editor with no history, and a copy of a Field shares the history of the one it was copied from.

## <a id="Field"></a>type Field

```go
type Field struct {
	// Value is the field's text.
	Value string
	// Caret is where the caret is: a count of characters from the start.
	// One past the end is the end.
	Caret int
	// Multiline is a textarea's or an editing host's: it has lines, and
	// the actions that only such fields have (hotty.Action.Multiline).
	Multiline bool
	// Password is a password input's: its value is one word.
	Password bool
	// Rows is how many rows the field shows, for page-up and page-down; 1
	// when less.
	Rows int
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Field is a text field's value, caret and selection.

### <a id="Field.Anchor"></a>func (*Field) Anchor

```go
func (f *Field) Anchor() (anchor int, ok bool)
```

Anchor is where the selection began, the end of it the caret is not at. ok is false when nothing is selected, and anchor is then the caret.

### <a id="Field.Do"></a>func (*Field) Do

```go
func (f *Field) Do(a hotty.Action) (changed bool)
```

Do does an action, and reports whether the value changed: then the program reports an input event. Submit and Program change nothing, the selection included; they are the program's to act on, and so are Copy, Cut and Paste: a Field keeps no clipboard (Paste is the pasted text's). Undo and Redo are the field's own history (from this version on; they were the program's), done by the keymap's bindings of them, so that a key the program binds to Program or to something else stays the program's. An action only a multi-line field has does nothing in an input.

A selection comes first (SPEC §10.2): a delete deletes it and nothing else; a move starts from its start when it goes back or up, and from its end otherwise, and ends it, and char-backward and char-forward stop there; select-all selects the whole value, the anchor at its start and the caret at its end.

### <a id="Field.Extend"></a>func (*Field) Extend

```go
func (f *Field) Extend(a hotty.Action) (changed bool)
```

Extend does a move as Shift does it (SPEC §10.2, Shift selects): the anchor stays, or is set where the caret is when nothing is selected, and the caret moves from where it is. When it comes back to the anchor, nothing is selected. An action that is not a move is Do's.

### <a id="Field.Key"></a>func (*Field) Key

```go
func (f *Field) Key(m *hotty.Keymap, key string) (a hotty.Action, changed bool)
```

Key does what a keymap says the field does with a key (hotty.Keymap's Lookup): it types a character, or does an action, with Extend when the keymap Selects with the key and with Do otherwise. It returns the action (hotty.Insert for a key that types, hotty.KeyText), "" when the key is not the field's, and whether the value changed.

#### <a id="example-Field.Key"></a>Example

A field in cells, edited with the keymap the program gives its surfaces.

```go
km := hotty.Resolve(hotty.Platform{}, false, hotty.TerminalKeys)
f := hottyedit.Field{Value: "hello wrld", Caret: 10}
f.Key(km, "alt+b")  // word-backward: hello |wrld
f.Key(km, "ctrl+f") // char-forward: hello w|rld
f.Key(km, "o")      // types it
fmt.Printf("%q %d\n", f.Value, f.Caret)
f.Key(km, "ctrl+w") // delete-word-backward
fmt.Printf("%q %d\n", f.Value, f.Caret)
f.Key(km, "shift+end") // line-end, selecting: hello [rld]
start, end := f.Selection()
fmt.Println(start, end)
f.Key(km, "shift+z") // types in place of the selection
fmt.Printf("%q %d\n", f.Value, f.Caret)
```

Output:

```
"hello world" 8
"hello rld" 6
6 9
"hello Z" 7
```

### <a id="Field.Paste"></a>func (*Field) Paste

```go
func (f *Field) Paste(text string) bool
```

Paste types pasted text in place of the selection, as one edit, and reports whether the value changed. The text is kept whole: CRLF and CR become LF and a tab four spaces. A field that has no lines (Multiline false) takes its line breaks as spaces.

### <a id="Field.Redo"></a>func (*Field) Redo

```go
func (f *Field) Redo() bool
```

Redo does again what Undo took back.

### <a id="Field.Select"></a>func (*Field) Select

```go
func (f *Field) Select(anchor, caret int)
```

Select selects from anchor to caret, as the user does with the pointer. Select(p, p) puts the caret at p, with nothing selected. It ends a run of row moves, as an action does.

### <a id="Field.Selection"></a>func (*Field) Selection

```go
func (f *Field) Selection() (start, end int)
```

Selection is the selection's start and end, in characters, for a rendition to draw: equal when nothing is selected.

### <a id="Field.Type"></a>func (*Field) Type

```go
func (f *Field) Type(text string) (changed bool)
```

Type types text in place of the selection, or at the caret, and reports whether the value changed. A character typed where the last was is of one step of the history with it.

### <a id="Field.Undo"></a>func (*Field) Undo

```go
func (f *Field) Undo() bool
```

Undo takes back the last edit, or the last run of typing, and reports whether there was one: the value and caret are as they were before it.
